title: SAGARMALA PROJECT, NATIONAL WATERWAYS AND COASTAL SHIPPING
body_text:
At the end of the 15th financial cycle, an independent third-party impact evaluation of the projects under the Sagarmala scheme was done by the National Productivity Council (NPC). These projects are under various pillars of Sagarmala scheme including port modernization, port connectivity, coastal community development and coastal shipping and inland waterways development. No project has been sanctioned for financial assistance under the port led industrialization pillar of Sagarmala scheme.
During financial year (FY) 2025-26, total cargo movement recorded on National Waterways (NWs) was 218 million metric tons. To promote the cargo traffic on National Waterways, a scheme (Jalvahak) for providing 35% incentive to cargo owners and introduction of scheduled service on NW-1 (Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly River System) and NW-2 (river Brahmaputra) and NW-16 (river Barak) via Indo Bangladesh Protocol by Inland & Coastal Shipping Limited (ICSL) has been approved by the Government.
The average turnaround time of Major Ports has improved to 48.84 hours in 2025-26 from 52.87 hours in FY 2021-22. The Container Port Performance Index (CPPI) published by the World Bank provides an objective and comparable assessment of container port performance based on the time vessels spend in port. As per the CPPI 2025, Jawaharlal Nehru Port ranked 22 nd , comparable with Hong Kong (9 th ), Singapore (21 st ), and Shanghai (23 rd ).
The policy initiatives taken by the Government to attract private investment in coastal shipping and inland water transport are under:
Coastal-shipping infrastructure is strengthened under Sagarmala scheme through coastal berths, Ro-Ro/Ro-Pax and passenger jetties, port-connectivity projects.
In the Union Budget 2026-27, a Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme has been announced to incentivize modal shift of cargo from road and rail to coastal shipping and inland waterways, with the objective of increasing their combined modal share from 6 per cent to 12 per cent by 2047. The scheme is expected to expand the addressable cargo base and generate opportunities for private investment in vessels, terminals, ship repair, cargo handling and multimodal logistics.
Development of National Waterway-5 (NW-5) in Odisha to connect the mineral-rich regions of Talcher and Angul with industrial centers such as Kalinga Nagar and with the ports of Paradip and Dhamra has been announced in the Union Budget 2026-27.
A scheme for providing 35% incentive to promote the utilization of inland waterways transport sector by cargo owners and for scheduled service for cargo movement on NW-1 and NW-2 and NW-16 via Indo Bangladesh Protocol by Inland & Coastal Shipping Limited (ICSL) has been approved by the Government.
An extension of the tonnage tax scheme to inland vessels registered under the Indian Vessels Act, 2021 was announced in the Union budget 2025-26 which has benefitted the Inland vessels operating on National Waterways, rivers, and canals.
The National Waterways (Construction of Jetties / Terminals) Regulations 2025 have been notified, allowing private companies to invest in and operate Inland Waterways terminals by providing a clear regulatory framework to attract private sector investment for facilitating the growth of inland waterways sector.
This information was given by the Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, in a written reply to the Rajya Sabha.

ministry.name: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

enrichment.summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways stated that the National Productivity Council conducted a third-party impact evaluation of Sagarmala scheme projects, with no projects sanctioned under its port-led industrialization pillar. National Waterways cargo movement reached 218 million metric tons in FY 2025-26, average turnaround time at Major Ports improved to 48.84 hours (from 52.87 hours in FY 2021-22), and Jawaharlal Nehru Port ranked 22nd in the World Bank's CPPI 2025. The Ministry also listed policy measures to boost coastal shipping and inland waterways, including the Jalvahak incentive scheme, the Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme (targeting 12% combined modal share by 2047), development of National Waterway-5 in Odisha, tonnage tax extension to inland vessels, and new regulations enabling private investment in inland waterway terminals.
enrichment.context:
Sagarmala is the Government of India's flagship program (launched 2015) for port-led development, aiming to modernize ports, improve port connectivity, promote port-led industrialization, and support coastal community development. Periodic third-party evaluations, like this one by the National Productivity Council, are used to assess scheme effectiveness and inform course corrections; the finding that no projects were sanctioned under the port-led industrialization pillar highlights a persistent implementation gap in that specific component. Inland Water Transport (IWT) and coastal shipping are being pushed as low-cost, environmentally efficient alternatives to road and rail freight, but currently contribute only about 6% of India's modal freight share, far below global benchmarks—hence the ambitious target of doubling this to 12% by 2047 (aligned with India@100 vision) through the newly announced Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme.

The mention of National Waterways-1, 2, and 16, the Jalvahak incentive scheme, and the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol Route reflects ongoing efforts to operationalize India's 111 declared National Waterways, most of which remain underutilized. The World Bank's Container Port Performance Index (CPPI) is a key global benchmark for port efficiency, and JNPT's improved ranking reflects broader port modernization efforts under Sagarmala and the Major Port Authorities Act, 2021. Extension of tonnage tax benefits (originally designed for ocean-going vessels under the Income Tax Act) to inland vessels, along with new terminal regulations under the Indian Vessels Act, 2021, signal a push to attract private capital into a historically public-sector-dominated inland shipping ecosystem.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding National Waterways in India:
1. National Waterway-1 covers the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system.
2. National Waterway-2 is on the river Brahmaputra.
3. National Waterway-16 connects via the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol Route on the river Barak.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, NW-1 is on the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system, NW-2 is on the river Brahmaputra, and NW-16 is on the river Barak connected via the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol Route. All three statements are correct.

prelims_questions.question: The Container Port Performance Index (CPPI), mentioned in the context of Jawaharlal Nehru Port's global ranking, is published by which organization?
options: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly states that the Container Port Performance Index (CPPI) is published by the World Bank to provide an objective assessment of container port performance based on vessel time spent in port.

mains_questions.question: Examine the objectives of the Sagarmala program and critically assess the challenges in achieving port-led industrialization in India.

Discuss the significance of promoting coastal shipping and inland waterways as alternatives to road and rail transport in India. Evaluate the policy measures announced in recent Union Budgets to achieve this modal shift.
